evals.prompt: /v-prompt-pack-generate — turn the plan I just wrote into prompt packs. The plan (PLAN_*.md from this session) adds a saved-filters feature to an existing app: a migration + ExampleFilter model, an ExampleFilterController with store/index/destroy, an Inertia React ExampleFilters page, a nav entry, and Pest feature tests. Laravel 13 + Inertia + React.
evals.expected_output: A .v-prompt-packs/<slug>-<MM-DD>/ dir in the canonical RUNNABLE form from v-runnable-pack-convention.md: FLAT wave-prefixed w<N>-*.txt packs (NOT wave subfolders — that shape is deprecated) plus a 00-README master map, with a 99-verify pack last. Step 1 grounding actually opens the files the plan references (migration dir, app/Models, app/Http/Controllers, resources/js/Pages, routes) before partitioning, and notes any drift or already-done items. Waves are sequenced by dependency: schema/model first, controller + routes next, React page after the controller exists, tests last; packs WITHIN a wave touch disjoint files so they are parallel-safe. Each pack is a self-contained /v prompt naming its exact file set and gate, ending 'leave staged; do not commit' — executable unattended via run-v-packs. No application code is written.

evals.prompt: /v-prompt-pack-generate on PLAN_tiny_fix.md — it's a one-line copy change in a single Blade view plus its test. Make prompt packs for it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the plan is below the parallelism threshold (~8h / 1-2 sessions, roughly <4 implementation tasks). Instead of emitting a full wave/pack tree, it emits a lightweight inline checklist, tells the operator the plan is too small to benefit from wave packs, and stops. Does not fabricate artificial waves for a trivial change.
